result.title: DuCo: Exploiting Dual Cross-Layer Consistency for Sparse Geometric Attention
result.summary: Dense global attention is crucial for capturing cross-view geometry in visual geometry foundation models, yet its quadratic complexity limits efficient inference on long image sequences. Existing sparse attention methods primarily select entries of the global attention matrix based on attention probabilities and construct masks independently across layers, overlooking value redundancy and cross-layer information reuse. By analyzing attention distributions and clustering value representations across layers, we reveal two forms of \emph{cross-layer consistency}, characterized by highly similar attention probability distributions and localized changes in value redundancy structures. Building on these observations, we propose \textbf{DuCo}, a training-free sparse attention framework that exploits historical attention information and value redundancy for efficient geometric inference. Specifically, DuCo leverages historical attention information to estimate current-layer dense attention probabilities and introduces value clustering to exploit redundancy, with clusters efficiently refined through local updates across layers. Both factors are integrated through probability-weighted value distortion to jointly optimize four cluster representation states under an attention budget for sparse mask construction. Experiments across three visual geometry foundation models and five benchmarks demonstrate favorable accuracy--efficiency trade-offs.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对视觉几何基础模型中稠密全局注意力的二次复杂度问题，分析出跨层注意力分布高度相似与 value 冗余结构局部变化两种一致性，并提出免训练稀疏注意力框架 DuCo：用历史注意力估计当前层概率、以 value 聚类刻画冗余，在注意力预算下联合构建稀疏掩码。
AI.relevance_reason: 其跨层注意力复用与 value 聚类在预算内筛选注意力条目的做法，可能为 LVR 中跨层注意力结构、缓存复用及视觉证据筛选的开销控制提供方法线索，但原文不涉及推理状态生成与答案使用，需核查迁移可行性。
